newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Victoria may restructure gas operations.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Victoria may restructure gas operations.

text.p: The state government of Victoria said on Tuesday it was considering restructuring its gas distribution and retailing groups into as many as seven new entities as part of ongoing gas sector reform.
As part of the process the government also was examining the privatisaton of a restructured industry to help reduce state debt and build competition, premier Jeff Kennett said in a statement.
State treasurer Alan Stockdale said the reforms would potentially create incentives for exploration and development of new commercial gas fields.

The government last month paid A$1 billion to Bass Strait oil and gas operators Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and Exxon Corp unit Esso Australia to settle a petroleum resource tax dispute which had hampered gas industry restructure plans.
Kennett said the government would consider restructuring state-owned distributor and retailer Gas and Fuel Corp (GASCOR) into two or three gas distribution and two to five retail businesses.
High pressure gas pipeleines owned and operated by the Gas Transmission Company would be retained in a single entity, he said.
Stockdale said the development of the final reform model for the gas industry would take several months.
Stockdale also announced that expressions of interest would shortly be called for the purchase of the 2000 megawatt Loy Yang A power station, Victoria's largest energy producer.
The privatisation of Loy Yang A would follow the successful sales of the Yallourn and Hazelwood power stations earlier this year for A$2.43 billion and A$2.35 billion respectively.
The state's electricity privatisation drive has netted a total of A$13.6 billion to date.
